question.:question/problem: Consider the positively (outward) oriented surface $S$ given by ${x}^{2}+(y-2)^{2}+(z+1)^{2}=25$ and the vector field $F=x\,i+xz\,j+3z\,k.$ Use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xz)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3z) \\  & =1+0+3 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $5$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}4\,\text{d}V \\  & =4{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =4\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {5}^{3} \\  & =\frac{2\,000\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186133930/plots/c70599f235e39863b300.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨2\left(3x+y{e}^{z}\right),\,2\left(xy+2\right),\,2\left(1-xz\right)⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of the rectangular solid shown above in the first octant. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\left(3x+y{e}^{z}\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\left(xy+2\right))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\left(1-xz\right)) \\  & =6+2 x+(- 2 x) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the rectangular solid enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}6\,\text{d}V \\  & =6{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =6\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =6\cdot 4\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =288.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\left(3x+y{e}^{z}\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\left(xy+2\right))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\left(1-xz\right)) \\  & =6+2 x+(- 2 x) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the rectangular solid enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}6\,\text{d}V \\  & =6{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =6\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =6\cdot 3\cdot 3\cdot 4 \\  & =216.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186133930/plots/51a9a61b578cc3f8edc2.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨3\left(1-2x\right),\,3\left(5y-3{z}^{2}\right),\,3\left({x}^{3}-{y}^{2}\right)⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of a right circular cylinder of height $4$ whose base is a circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin, as shown above. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3\left(1-2x\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3\left(5y-3{z}^{2}\right))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3\left({x}^{3}-{y}^{2}\right)) \\  & =(-6)+15+0 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid cylinder enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}9\,\text{d}V \\  & =9{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =9\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =9\cdot \pi \cdot {2}^{2}\cdot 4 \\  & =144 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3\left(yz-2x\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3\left(3y\right))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3\left(x+z\right)) \\  & =(-6)+9+3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $5$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}6\,\text{d}V \\  & =6{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =6\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {5}^{3} \\  & =1000 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}+4xy)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(5y-2{y}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(6xz) \\  & =-6x+4y+(5-4y)+6x \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $3$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}5\,\text{d}V \\  & =5{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =5\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {3}^{3} \\  & =180 \pi.\end{aligned}
$$
